newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00 cent higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00 cent higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 1.00 cent higher Monday as traders expect the market to follow through on Friday's firm finish.

New York arabica prices ended higher in light trade Friday, bolstered by local and speculative buying. September settled up 3.85 cents at 164.30 cents a lb after ranging from 167.00 to 159.75. Spot July, which expires today, ended 5.60 cents higher at 192.50 cents, while the outer months closed up 2.60 to down 0.30.
The July/September switch widened to 28.20 cents compared with 26.45 cents at the close on Thursday, while September/December stretched to 12.85 cents from 14.20 cents.

Technically, traders pegged September resistance at 167.00-168.00 cents, with the next level seen near 170.00. Buy-stops were said to be building around 175.00. On the downside, support was put at 160.00, then 158.00.
After Friday's close, CSCE reported that certified coffee inventories rose by 3,441 60-kg bags as of July 17, to 80,592 bags. An additional 11,479 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.
CSCE also reported that 31,787 bags of coffee were graded and only 8,478 bags had passed exchange approval.

On the weather front, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Monday that there is no damaging cold weather expected this week in Brazil's coffee belt, with low temperatures in major coffee-growing areas expected to be in the low 50s (low to middle teens C).

The CFTC Commitments of Traders report released after Friday's close showed non-commercial long postions in the two weeks ending July 15 fell by 385 lots, to 3,174 lots. Non-commercial short positions rose by 453 lots, to 1,636 lots.
Commercial long positions rose by 793 lots in the two weeks, to 8,418 lots, while commercial short positions fell by 1,482 lots, to 10,815 lots.
Nonreportable long positions decreased by 217 lots to 8,363 lots and nonreportable short positions increased by 1,220 lots to 7,504 lots.
London robusta futures were flat to firmer in exceedingly thin trade early Monday. At the midday break, benchmark September rose $3 to $1,608, after ranging from $1,610 to $1,590.
